newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banacci to go it alone on pensions.
newsitem.headline: Banacci to go it alone on pensions.

text.p: Banamex-Accival (Banacci), Mexico's largest banking group, will not be looking for a partner for its pension fund management firm, Afore Banamex, officials said on Thursday.

Officials told a news conference that the Afore, as the pension management firms are called in Mexico, would be headed by Banacci official Jose Marron, who would step down from his position on the executive committee of the group.

"We don't need a partner," said Manuel Medina Mora, head of Banacci, noting that the banking group already had experience running pension funds in South America, and had a strong foothold in the government-run Retirement Savings System that currently operates in Mexico.
Other top Mexican banks have already set up partnerships with foreign firms to run their Afores.
Mexico is due to pass pension fund management into private-sector hands in January 1997, but President Ernesto Zedillo has not yet signed the rules under which the new system will operate.
